commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy, rename, move or trash a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: turnaround-detector
commands.description: Deep financial execution analysis to identify turnaround and growth companies for investment. Use whenever the user asks about turnaround stocks, management execution quality, OCF vs profit quality, CCC analysis, working capital trends, ROCE improvement, or whether a company is genuinely improving. Trigger for ANY @tradeidea investment analysis request covering IT/tech, banks, EPC/infrastructure, or cables/power sector. Trigger when @tradeidea is mentioned with phrases like review, investment perspective, do an analysis, order book, expansion, management review, or headwinds. Also trigger for is this company turning around, check management execution, is the quality of earnings real, find value in beaten-down stocks. Runs a 5-dimension scorecard covering earnings quality, operational efficiency, balance sheet health, ROCE, and smart money signals. Adds sector-specific KPIs, headwind/tailwind analysis, valuation scenarios, and generates a publishable MD report with dual disclaimers. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

1	---
2	
3	description: "Task list for 001-gis-scorer (GIS Scorer, deterministic General Investor Score)"
4	---
5	
6	# Tasks: GIS Scorer (deterministic General Investor Score)
7	
8	**Input**: Design documents from `specs/001-gis-scorer/`: [plan.md](plan.md), [spec.md](spec.md),
9	[research.md](research.md), [data-model.md](data-model.md), [contracts/](contracts/),
10	[quickstart.md](quickstart.md); constitution `.specify/memory/constitution.md` v1.0.0.
11	
12	**Tests**: REQUIRED (Constitution III, test-first, NON-NEGOTIABLE). In every phase the test tasks
13	come before the implementation tasks, and a "confirm red" task records that tests of
14	not-yet-implemented behaviour fail before that behaviour is written, listing any that pass because
15	the behaviour already exists. Every test task names the FR / acceptance-scenario (`USn-ASm`) / SC
16	ids it verifies, and those ids MUST appear in the test function names or docstrings (research
17	R-12), so the traceability check (written in T011a, completed in T075) can find them.
18	
19	**Validation decisions**: research.md R-01 (explicit `null`, null list elements, empty list) and
20	R-02 (integral-float Piotroski, booleans rejected) are **CONFIRMED by Balaji (2026-11-22)** and recorded in spec.md Clarifications.
21	Every test that depends on them carries the literal tag `R-01` or `R-02`
22	in its docstring (they are already in spec.md Clarifications; no task edits the spec).
23	
24	**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story is an independently testable
25	increment. All paths are relative to `Assignment-1/Part-1A/`. All Python commands use
26	`.venv/bin/…` (Constitution, Technical Constraints).
27	
28	## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`
29	
30	- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
31	- **[Story]**: The user story the task belongs to (US1…US6)
32	- **Checking off red-phase tasks (Constitution III)**: test-writing tasks and confirm-red tasks
33	  end with a deliberately failing suite. They are recorded in the task log when done, but they are
34	  checked off (`[x]`) only together with their phase's green-run task, once the full suite
35	  passes: Phase 1 T007 and Phase 2 T008–T012 with T016; US1 T017–T029 with T039; US2 T040–T044 with
36	  T048; US3 T049–T051 with T053; US4 T054–T056 with T059; US5 T060–T062 with T064; US6 T065–T069
37	  with T072; Phase 9 T073–T076 with T079.
38	
39	## Conventions used by the tasks (from plan.md, research.md, data-model.md)
40	
41	- **Modules** (plan.md Project Structure): `src/gis_scorer/{__init__,__main__,cli,snapshot,rules,scoring,valuation,result}.py`.
42	- **Internal API the tests call** (contracts/library-api.md allows tests to import internals):
43	  - `gis_scorer.snapshot`: `FIELDS` (tuple of the 30 field names in data-model.md §1 order),
44	    `Snapshot`, `validate(raw) -> Snapshot`, `FieldError`, `SnapshotValidationError`.
45	  - `gis_scorer.rules`: `Ladder`, `apply_ladder(ladder, value)`, `GrowthOutcome`,
46	    `compute_growth(current, prior) -> GrowthOutcome`, one item scorer per catalogue row
47	    `score_<item>(snapshot: Snapshot) -> ScoreItem`: `score_piotroski`, `score_altman_z`,
48	    `score_beneish_m`, `score_ebitda_growth`, `score_earnings_growth`, `score_revenue_growth`,
49	    `score_equity_growth`, `score_cash_flow_quality`, `score_net_profit_margin`,
50	    `score_operating_margin`, `score_roe`, `score_roce`, `score_loss_to_profit`,
51	    `score_profitability_sustainability`, `score_working_capital`, `score_debt_reduction`,
52	    `score_current_ratio`, `score_debt_to_equity`; and `score_penalties(snapshot) -> tuple[ScoreItem, ...]`.
53	  - `gis_scorer.scoring`: `compute_total(earned: int, available: int) -> int`,
54	    `decide_label(total: int, dimensions: tuple[Dimension, ...], snapshot: Snapshot) -> LabelDecision`,
55	    `score_snapshot(raw) -> ScoreResult`.
56	  - `gis_scorer.valuation`: `score_valuation(snapshot: Snapshot) -> Valuation`.
57	- **Constants**: every threshold/points value is a module constant named `FRxxx_*` (research R-03).
58	- **Test names**: unit `test_frNNN_<behaviour>`, acceptance `test_usN_asM_<behaviour>` with a
59	  docstring starting `"USn-ASm: …"`, parametrize ids like `fr010_ge8_at_8` / `fr010_ge8_below_7`
60	  (research R-12). Every test module has a unique basename (pytest default import mode).
61	- **Float boundaries**: when a boundary test derives its input from a subtraction or a growth
62	  formula, it first asserts the derived value equals the intended boundary exactly (a precondition
63	  assert), so floating-point noise can never silently move a case to the wrong side.
64	- **Staged assembly** (keeps every story independently testable): `decide_label` gains FR-052 in
65	  US1, FR-051 in US2 and FR-053–FR-055 in US3; `score_valuation` is created in US1 with only the
66	  FR-060 missing-input path and gains its bands in US5; the Penalties dimension is empty until US4.
67	- **Traceability scope** (Constitution workflow gate "traceability stays complete"): the environment
68	  variable `GIS_TRACE_SCOPE` holds comma-separated tokens from the table below. The traceability
69	  test (T011a) expects the union of their ids. Unset means full scope: every FR and every
70	  `USn-ASm` in spec.md. Each phase's green-run task sets it to `foundation` plus every story whose
71	  green run has passed, including its own. The values shown in the green-run tasks assume the order
72	  US1 → US6; add any story completed out of that order.
73	
74	  | Token | FR ids | Acceptance scenarios |
75	  |---|---|---|
76	  | `foundation` | FR-001, FR-070, FR-071 | — |
77	  | `US1` | FR-003, FR-010 – FR-027, FR-030, FR-044, FR-050, FR-052 | US1-AS1 … US1-AS5 |
78	  | `US2` | FR-002, FR-051 | US2-AS1 … US2-AS4 |
79	  | `US3` | FR-053, FR-054, FR-055 | US3-AS1 … US3-AS5 |
80	  | `US4` | FR-040, FR-041, FR-042, FR-043 | US4-AS1 … US4-AS4 |
81	  | `US5` | FR-060 | US5-AS1 … US5-AS3 |
82	  | `US6` | FR-072 | US6-AS1, US6-AS2 |
83	
84	---
85	
86	## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)
87	
88	**Purpose**: Packaging, pinned dev tools in `Part-1A/.venv`, and the harness.
89	
90	- [ ] T001 Create the directory skeleton from plan.md Project Structure: `src/gis_scorer/`, `tests/unit/`, `tests/acceptance/`, `tests/fixtures/snapshots/`, `.harness/` (empty directories only; no `__init__.py` under `tests/`)
91	- [ ] T002 Create `pyproject.toml` per research.md R-08: `[build-system] requires = ["setuptools>=77"]`, `build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"`; `[project] name = "gis-scorer"`, `version = "0.1.0"`, `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, `dependencies = []`; `[project.scripts] gis-scorer = "gis_scorer.cli:main"`; `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["src"]`; `[tool.ruff] target-version = "py312"`, `line-length = 100`; `[tool.ruff.lint] select = ["E","F","W","I","B","UP","SIM"]`; `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths = ["tests"]`; `[tool.coverage.run] source = ["gis_scorer"]`, `branch = true`; `[tool.coverage.report] show_missing = true`. (`python -m gis_scorer` is provided by `src/gis_scorer/__main__.py` in T071.)
92	- [ ] T003 [P] Create minimal `src/gis_scorer/__init__.py` containing only `__version__ = "0.1.0"` and a module docstring, so the editable install in T006 succeeds (public re-exports are added in T038)
93	- [ ] T004 [P] Create `requirements-dev.txt` with the exact pins from research.md R-09, one per line: `ruff==0.14.0`, `bandit==1.8.6`, `pytest==8.4.2`, `pytest-cov==7.0.0` (no ranges)
94	- [ ] T005 [P] Create `.harness/run_harness.sh` exactly per contracts/harness.md and research.md R-10: bash, `set -u` and `set -o pipefail` but **not** `set -e`; `cd` to `Part-1A` from the script's own location; call tools only via `.venv/bin/`; create `evidence/harness-results/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)/`; run steps `1a-ruff-check` (`ruff check .`), `1b-ruff-format` (`ruff format --check .`), `2-bandit` (`bandit -r src -ll`), `3-pytest` (`pytest --cov=gis_scorer --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=90`), each to its own `<step-id>.log` (stdout+stderr) with its exit code captured; write `environment.txt` (`python --version`, `pip freeze`, `git rev-parse HEAD` or `no commit`) and `summary.md` (table: step id | command | exit code | PASS/FAIL; then Gate 1/2/3 results, Gate 1 = 1a AND 1b; then `OVERALL: PASS|FAIL`); last output line prints the evidence directory and the overall result; exit 0 only if all gates pass, else 1. `chmod +x` the script.
95	- [ ] T006 Install into `Part-1A/.venv` (depends on T002–T004): `.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` then `.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e .`; verify with `.venv/bin/ruff --version`, `.venv/bin/bandit --version`, `.venv/bin/pytest --version`, `.venv/bin/python -m pip show pytest-cov`, `.venv/bin/python -c "import gis_scorer; print(gis_scorer.__version__)"`. If a pin fails to install or run on Python 3.14, bump it to the nearest later working release in `requirements-dev.txt` and record the change under R-09 in `specs/001-gis-scorer/research.md`

[quickstart.md](quickstart.md); constitution `.specify/memory/constitution.md` v1.0.0.

**Tests**: REQUIRED (Constitution III, test-first, NON-NEGOTIABLE). In every phase the test tasks
come before the implementation tasks, and a "confirm red" task records that tests of
not-yet-implemented behaviour fail before that behaviour is written, listing any that pass because
the behaviour already exists. Every test task names the FR / acceptance-scenario (`USn-ASm`) / SC
ids it verifies, and those ids MUST appear in the test function names or docstrings (research
R-12), so the traceability check (written in T011a, completed in T075) can find them.

**Validation decisions**: research.md R-01 (explicit `null`, null list elements, empty list) and
R-02 (integral-float Piotroski, booleans rejected) are **CONFIRMED by Balaji (2026-11-22)** and recorded in spec.md Clarifications.
Every test that depends on them carries the literal tag `R-01` or `R-02`
in its docstring (they are already in spec.md Clarifications; no task edits the spec).

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story is an independently testable
increment. All paths are relative to `Assignment-1/Part-1A/`. All Python commands use
`.venv/bin/…` (Constitution, Technical Constraints).

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: The user story the task belongs to (US1…US6)
- **Checking off red-phase tasks (Constitution III)**: test-writing tasks and confirm-red tasks
  end with a deliberately failing suite. They are recorded in the task log when done, but they are
  checked off (`[x]`) only together with their phase's green-run task, once the full suite
  passes: Phase 1 T007 and Phase 2 T008–T012 with T016; US1 T017–T029 with T039; US2 T040–T044 with
  T048; US3 T049–T051 with T053; US4 T054–T056 with T059; US5 T060–T062 with T064; US6 T065–T069
  with T072; Phase 9 T073–T076 with T079.

## Conventions used by the tasks (from plan.md, research.md, data-model.md)

- **Modules** (plan.md Project Structure): `src/gis_scorer/{__init__,__main__,cli,snapshot,rules,scoring,valuation,result}.py`.
- **Internal API the tests call** (contracts/library-api.md allows tests to import internals):
  - `gis_scorer.snapshot`: `FIELDS` (tuple of the 30 field names in data-model.md §1 order),
    `Snapshot`, `validate(raw) -> Snapshot`, `FieldError`, `SnapshotValidationError`.
  - `gis_scorer.rules`: `Ladder`, `apply_ladder(ladder, value)`, `GrowthOutcome`,
    `compute_growth(current, prior) -> GrowthOutcome`, one item scorer per catalogue row
    `score_<item>(snapshot: Snapshot) -> ScoreItem`: `score_piotroski`, `score_altman_z`,
    `score_beneish_m`, `score_ebitda_growth`, `score_earnings_growth`, `score_revenue_growth`,
    `score_equity_growth`, `score_cash_flow_quality`, `score_net_profit_margin`,
    `score_operating_margin`, `score_roe`, `score_roce`, `score_loss_to_profit`,
    `score_profitability_sustainability`, `score_working_capital`, `score_debt_reduction`,
    `score_current_ratio`, `score_debt_to_equity`; and `score_penalties(snapshot) -> tuple[ScoreItem, ...]`.
  - `gis_scorer.scoring`: `compute_total(earned: int, available: int) -> int`,
    `decide_label(total: int, dimensions: tuple[Dimension, ...], snapshot: Snapshot) -> LabelDecision`,
    `score_snapshot(raw) -> ScoreResult`.
  - `gis_scorer.valuation`: `score_valuation(snapshot: Snapshot) -> Valuation`.
- **Constants**: every threshold/points value is a module constant named `FRxxx_*` (research R-03).
- **Test names**: unit `test_frNNN_<behaviour>`, acceptance `test_usN_asM_<behaviour>` with a
  docstring starting `"USn-ASm: …"`, parametrize ids like `fr010_ge8_at_8` / `fr010_ge8_below_7`
  (research R-12). Every test module has a unique basename (pytest default import mode).
- **Float boundaries**: when a boundary test derives its input from a subtraction or a growth
  formula, it first asserts the derived value equals the intended boundary exactly (a precondition
  assert), so floating-point noise can never silently move a case to the wrong side.
- **Staged assembly** (keeps every story independently testable): `decide_label` gains FR-052 in
  US1, FR-051 in US2 and FR-053–FR-055 in US3; `score_valuation` is created in US1 with only the
  FR-060 missing-input path and gains its bands in US5; the Penalties dimension is empty until US4.
- **Traceability scope** (Constitution workflow gate "traceability stays complete"): the environment
  variable `GIS_TRACE_SCOPE` holds comma-separated tokens from the table below. The traceability
  test (T011a) expects the union of their ids. Unset means full scope: every FR and every
  `USn-ASm` in spec.md. Each phase's green-run task sets it to `foundation` plus every story whose
  green run has passed, including its own. The values shown in the green-run tasks assume the order
  US1 → US6; add any story completed out of that order.

  | Token | FR ids | Acceptance scenarios |
  |---|---|---|
  | `foundation` | FR-001, FR-070, FR-071 | — |
  | `US1` | FR-003, FR-010 – FR-027, FR-030, FR-044, FR-050, FR-052 | US1-AS1 … US1-AS5 |
  | `US2` | FR-002, FR-051 | US2-AS1 … US2-AS4 |
  | `US3` | FR-053, FR-054, FR-055 | US3-AS1 … US3-AS5 |
  | `US4` | FR-040, FR-041, FR-042, FR-043 | US4-AS1 … US4-AS4 |
  | `US5` | FR-060 | US5-AS1 … US5-AS3 |
  | `US6` | FR-072 | US6-AS1, US6-AS2 |

1	# Feature Specification: GIS Scorer (deterministic General Investor Score)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `001-gis-scorer`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-11-22
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "A new, small, deterministic module that re-implements the General
10	Investor Score (GIS) method from myportfolio-web: given one company's pre-computed financial
11	metrics, return a 0–100 quality score, its per-dimension breakdown, a recommendation label and a
12	separate 0–10 valuation score. Scope is the subset of GIS that can be computed from explicit inputs
13	alone (see GIS_REFERENCE.md §7)."
14	
15	## Clarifications
16	
17	### Session 2026-11-22
18	
19	Decisions confirmed by the project owner (Balaji); non-interactive session.
20	
21	- Q: Which companies and which parts of the reference GIS method are in scope? → A: Non-financial
22	  companies only (banks, NBFCs and insurers are out of scope). Scoring ladders are fixed, with no
23	  sector-percentile thresholds. Out of scope: Capital Deployment and its re-weighting, red-flag
24	  penalties, other-income divergence, core-profit substitution, growth acceleration, the QoQ
25	  momentum items, NPM-improving-YoY, and any database or data fetching.
26	- Q: Is an input of exactly zero a real value or missing data? → A: Zero is a real value and is
27	  scored as such, including ROE, ROCE, P/E, P/B and PEG; only an absent value is missing.
28	- Q: What happens when the input is invalid (unknown field, non-numeric, non-finite or out of
29	  range)? → A: Scoring is refused with an error that names the field.
30	- Q: What makes the quality gate fail, and does it include a red-flag check? → A: There is no
31	  red-flag check; the gate fails only on ROE missing, ROE < 12%, or Piotroski < 4.
32	- Q: How is the total rounded to a whole number? → A: To the nearest integer, ties to even.
33	- Q: Is an explicit null the same as an omitted field, and what do a null element or an empty list
34	  in `recent_net_profit_margins` mean? → A: Explicit null is the same as absent (missing). A null
35	  element stops the run of consecutive profitable quarters. An empty list means no quarter was
36	  supplied, so Profitability Sustainability is 0 of 0. (Raised by /speckit-clarify; confirmed by
37	  Balaji in the project thread, 2026-11-22.)
38	- Q: Does a whole-number float count as an integer for Piotroski, and are booleans numeric? → A:
39	  `6.0` is accepted as 6; `6.5` is rejected; booleans are rejected as non-numeric in every field.
40	  (Raised by /speckit-clarify; confirmed by Balaji in the project thread, 2026-11-22.)
41	
42	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
43	
44	The user is an analyst (or a program acting for one) who has a company's financial metrics and
45	wants a reproducible, explainable quality score for it.
46	
47	### User Story 1 - Score a company and get its total (Priority: P1)
48	
49	The analyst supplies one company's metric snapshot and receives a total score from 0 to 100, plus
50	a breakdown showing, for every scoring item, the points earned, the points available, and the
51	rule that was applied.
52	
53	**Why this priority**: The total and its breakdown are the core of the method; every other story
54	builds on them.
55	
56	**Independent Test**: Supply a complete snapshot with known values and check every item's points,
57	each dimension's subtotal and the normalised total against hand-computed figures.
58	
59	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
60	
61	1. **Given** a snapshot where every input is present and every item earns its maximum,
62	   **When** it is scored, **Then** the total is 100 and no penalty is listed.
63	2. **Given** a snapshot with Piotroski 6, Altman Z 2.5 and Beneish M −2.5, **When** it is scored,
64	   **Then** Forensic Quality shows 7/10, 3/5 and 5/5 (15 of 20).
65	3. **Given** revenue for the last 12 months of 115 against 100 for the 12 months before,
66	   **When** it is scored, **Then** revenue growth is 15% and earns 7 of 10.
67	4. **Given** a snapshot whose prior-12-month EBITDA is 0, **When** it is scored, **Then** EBITDA
68	   growth is reported as "capped" and earns the fixed 4 of 8, and no EBITDA decline penalty applies.
69	5. **Given** raw points of 45 earned out of 90 available, **When** the total is computed,
70	   **Then** the total is 50.
71	
72	---
73	
74	### User Story 2 - Missing data is excluded, never zeroed (Priority: P1)
75	
76	The analyst often has incomplete data. A missing metric must not drag the score down as if it were
77	zero; it must drop out of both the earned and the available points, and the breakdown must say
78	"no data" for it.
79	
80	**Why this priority**: Wrong handling of missing data silently corrupts every score, so it is as
81	critical as scoring itself.
82	
83	**Independent Test**: Score the same snapshot with and without one input; the item disappears from
84	the available points and the total is re-normalised over what remains.
85	
86	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
87	
88	1. **Given** a snapshot with no Altman Z value, **When** it is scored, **Then** the Altman item
89	   shows 0 of 0 with reason "No data" and Forensic Quality is out of 15, not 20.
90	2. **Given** a snapshot with ROE exactly 0, **When** it is scored, **Then** ROE is scored as a real
91	   value (0 of 5), not treated as missing.
92	3. **Given** a snapshot where nothing at all can be scored, **When** it is scored, **Then** the
93	   total is 0 and the label is SUSPICIOUS.
94	4. **Given** an input that is not a number, is infinite, or is outside its allowed range (for
95	   example Piotroski 11), **When** it is scored, **Then** scoring is refused with an error naming
96	   the field, and no partial result is returned.
97	
98	---
99	
100	### User Story 3 - Get a recommendation label I can trust (Priority: P2)
101	
102	The analyst wants a plain label (STRONG BUY … STRONG SELL) derived from the total, but a positive
103	label must not be shown when the data behind it is thin or the business fails basic quality checks.
104	
105	**Why this priority**: The label is what most users read; it depends on the total being right first.
106	
107	**Independent Test**: Feed totals on each side of each label boundary, then positive-band snapshots
108	that are missing a core dimension or fail the quality gate.
109	
110	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
111	
112	1. **Given** totals of 70, 69, 55, 54, 40, 39, 25 and 24 with complete data that passes the quality
113	   gate, **When** labelled,
114	   **Then** the labels are STRONG BUY, BUY, BUY, HOLD, HOLD, SELL, SELL, STRONG SELL.
115	2. **Given** a total of 80 but no ROE and no ROCE, **When** labelled, **Then** the label is
116	   INSUFFICIENT DATA and the reason names the missing dimension.
117	3. **Given** a total of 80 with complete data and ROE 10%, **When** labelled, **Then** the label is
118	   HOLD and the reason says ROE is below 12%.
119	4. **Given** a snapshot with no net profit margin, **When** labelled, **Then** the label is
120	   SUSPICIOUS whatever the total.
121	5. **Given** a total of 30, missing ROE and ROCE, **When** labelled, **Then** the label stays SELL
122	   (gates only ever downgrade positive labels).
123	
124	---
125	
126	### User Story 4 - Penalties for a deteriorating business (Priority: P2)
127	
128	The analyst wants declining revenue, earnings or EBITDA, and shrinking margins, to cost points,
129	and wants to see each penalty listed.
130	
131	**Why this priority**: Penalties change the total materially and are a frequent source of disputes.
132	
133	**Independent Test**: Score a snapshot with declining figures and check each penalty line and the
134	effect on the total.
135	
136	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
137	
138	1. **Given** revenue growth of −2%, **When** scored, **Then** a "Revenue Declining" penalty of −5
139	   is listed and revenue growth itself earns 0 of 10.
140	2. **Given** net margin 8% vs 9% a year earlier and operating margin 12% vs 13% a year earlier,
141	   **When** scored, **Then** a "Margin Compression" penalty of −3 is listed.
142	3. **Given** only one of the two margins below its year-ago value, **When** scored, **Then** no
143	   Margin Compression penalty is listed.
144	4. **Given** penalties that push raw points below zero, **When** the total is computed, **Then** the
145	   total is 0, never negative.
146	
147	---
148	
149	### User Story 5 - Separate valuation score (Priority: P3)
150	
151	The analyst wants a 0–10 valuation score from P/E, P/B and PEG, reported separately so price never
152	changes the quality score.
153	
154	**Why this priority**: Useful context, but independent of the quality score.
155	
156	**Independent Test**: Score P/E, P/B and PEG values on each side of each band and check the sum.
157	
158	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
159	
160	1. **Given** P/E 11, P/B 1.4 and PEG 0.9, **When** valued, **Then** the valuation score is 10.
161	2. **Given** P/E 60, P/B 4 and PEG 2, **When** valued, **Then** the valuation score is 0.
162	3. **Given** no P/E, P/B or PEG, **When** valued, **Then** the valuation score is 0 and the quality
163	   total is unchanged.
164	
165	---
166	
167	### User Story 6 - Run it from the command line (Priority: P3)
168	
169	The analyst wants to score a snapshot stored in a file without writing code, and get the result
170	as structured output.
171	
172	**Why this priority**: Convenience for the harness and demos; the library is the product.
173	
174	**Independent Test**: Run the command on a sample snapshot file and compare its output with the
175	library's result for the same input.
176	
177	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
178	
179	1. **Given** a valid snapshot file, **When** the command is run on it, **Then** it prints the result
180	   as structured data and exits successfully.
181	2. **Given** an invalid snapshot file, **When** the command is run on it, **Then** it prints the
182	   validation error and exits with a failure status.
183	
184	---
185	
186	### Edge Cases
187	
188	- A growth base (prior 12 months) of zero or negative → the item is "capped" (fixed mid points),
189	  never a division by zero, and no decline penalty applies to it.
190	- Current value more than 4× its base → "capped" (a recovery or base effect, not real growth).
191	- Exactly 4× the base → not capped (the cap test is strictly greater than 4×); values are rounded to
192	  6 decimal places before this test so tiny floating-point noise cannot flip it.
193	- Negative current value against a positive base → normal growth (negative %), scored and penalised.
194	- Total exactly on a half point (e.g. 72.5) → rounded half to even (72), matching the reference.
195	- Operating cash flow ÷ net profit below 0 while TTM profit is positive → −3 (worse than 0).
196	  The same ratio when TTM profit is a loss or unknown, or a ratio of exactly 0 → 0.
197	- A negative P/E (loss-making company) is scored as given, so it falls in the cheapest band; callers
198	  should pass P/E as missing for a loss-maker, as the reference's data does.
199	- D/E below 0.5 in both years → Debt Reduction is not applicable (0 of 0), not 0 of 3.
200	- Working capital with only CCC or only DSO available → the missing change counts as 0 and the
201	  item is still scored; with neither → 0 of 0.
202	- Profitability Sustainability with fewer than 2 quarters supplied → 0 of 2 (scored, not missing)
203	  unless no quarter is supplied at all.
204	- Piotroski must be an integer 0–9; anything else is an input error.
205	- An unknown field name, a non-numeric value, a non-finite value (NaN, ±infinity) or an
206	  out-of-range value → scoring is refused with an error naming the field; nothing is scored.
207	- ROE or ROCE of exactly 0 → scored as 0 of 5 (not missing). P/E, P/B or PEG of exactly 0 → scored
208	  in its lowest band (P/E 5, P/B 3, PEG 2), not treated as missing.
209	
210	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
211	
212	### Functional Requirements
213	
214	**Inputs and validation**
215	
216	- **FR-001**: The system MUST accept one company snapshot made of the named metrics in the Key
217	  Entities section. Every metric is optional; only an absent value (or an explicit null, which is the same) means "missing". Zero is a real
218	  value and is scored as such for every metric, including ROE, ROCE, P/E, P/B and PEG.
219	- **FR-002**: The system MUST reject a snapshot containing an unknown field, a non-numeric value, a
220	  non-finite value, or a value outside its stated range, with an error that names the field.
221	- **FR-003**: The system MUST produce identical output for identical input, with no dependence on
222	  time, environment, files, network or randomness.
223	
224	**Item scoring**: each item yields points earned, points available and a reason. A missing input
225	gives 0 of 0 with reason "No data". All boundaries below are exact.
226	
227	- **FR-010 Piotroski F-score** (available 10): ≥8 → 10; ≥6 → 7; ≥4 → 4; ≥2 → 2; otherwise 0.
228	- **FR-011 Altman Z** (5): >2.99 → 5; ≥1.81 → 3; otherwise 0.
229	- **FR-012 Beneish M** (5): <−2.22 → 5; ≤−1.78 → 2; otherwise 0.
230	- **FR-013 Growth calculation**: For revenue, EBITDA and net profit, growth % =
231	  (current 12M − prior 12M) ÷ |prior 12M| × 100, both values first rounded to 6 decimals. If the
232	  prior 12M is ≤ 0, or the current 12M is > 0 and greater than 4 × prior 12M, the growth is
233	  "capped" and no percentage is reported. If either value is missing, growth is missing.
234	- **FR-014 EBITDA growth** (8): ≥20% → 8; ≥15 → 6; ≥10 → 4; ≥5 → 2; otherwise 0. Capped → 4 of 8.
235	- **FR-015 Earnings (net profit) growth** (7): ≥20% → 7; ≥10 → 5; ≥5 → 3; ≥0 → 2; otherwise 0.
236	  Capped → 3 of 7.
237	- **FR-016 Revenue growth** (10): ≥25% → 10; ≥15 → 7; ≥10 → 5; ≥0 → 3; otherwise 0.
238	  Capped → 5 of 10.
239	- **FR-017 Equity growth** (5), from current and prior equity, growth = (current − prior) ÷ |prior|
240	  × 100, missing if prior is 0: >15% → 5; ≥10 → 3; ≥5 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
241	- **FR-018 Cash-flow quality** (5), operating cash flow ÷ net profit: ≥1.5 → 5; ≥1.0 → 4; ≥0.8 → 3;
242	  ≥0.5 → 2; >0 → 1; <0 with TTM net profit (`net_profit_12m`) > 0 → −3; otherwise 0.
243	- **FR-019 Net profit margin** (3): >15% → 3; >10 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
244	- **FR-020 Operating margin** (4): >20% → 4; >15 → 3; >10 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
245	- **FR-021 ROE and ROCE** (5 each): ≥15% → 5; ≥12 → 3; ≥8 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
246	- **FR-022 Loss → Profit transition** (5): available when current and previous net margin are both
247	  present; 5 when current > 0 and previous ≤ 0, otherwise 0.
248	- **FR-023 Profitability sustainability** (2): count the consecutive quarters, newest first, with net
249	  margin > 0 (stopping at the first that is not, or is missing); ≥4 → 2; ≥2 → 1; otherwise 0.
250	  Missing only when no quarterly margin is supplied (field absent, null, or an empty list).
251	- **FR-024 Working-capital efficiency** (5): ΔCCC = current − prior CCC days; ΔDSO = current − prior
252	  DSO days; a change that cannot be computed counts as 0, and the item is missing when neither can.
253	  ΔCCC ≤ −300 or ΔDSO ≤ −40 → 5; ΔCCC ≤ −150 or ΔDSO ≤ −25 → 4; ΔCCC ≤ −75 or ΔDSO ≤ −12 → 3;
254	  ΔCCC ≤ −30 or ΔDSO ≤ −5 → 2; ΔCCC < 0 or ΔDSO < 0 → 1; otherwise 0.
255	- **FR-025 Debt reduction** (3): needs current and prior D/E. If both are < 0.5 → 0 of 0 ("not
256	  applicable"). Otherwise ΔD/E = current − prior: ≤ −0.5 → 3; ≤ −0.2 → 2; < 0 → 1; otherwise 0.
257	- **FR-026 Current ratio** (5): >2.0 → 5; ≥1.5 → 3; ≥1.0 → 1; otherwise 0.
258	- **FR-027 Debt-to-equity level** (5): <0.5 → 5; ≤1.0 → 3; ≤2.0 → 1; otherwise 0.
259	
260	**Dimensions**
261	
262	- **FR-030**: Items MUST be grouped and reported in this order:
263	  Forensic Quality (FR-010–012), Growth (FR-014–015), Revenue Quality (FR-016),
264	  Financial Health (FR-017–018), Profitability (FR-019–020), Competitive Moat (FR-021),
265	  Turnaround (FR-022–025), Balance Sheet (FR-026–027), Penalties (FR-040–043).
266	  Each dimension reports the sum of its items' earned and available points.
267	
268	**Penalties**: points < 0 with 0 available.
269	
270	- **FR-040**: Revenue growth < 0 → "Revenue Declining" −5.
271	- **FR-041**: Earnings growth < 0 → "Earnings Declining" −5.
272	- **FR-042**: EBITDA growth < 0 → "EBITDA Declining" −5.
273	- **FR-043**: Net margin below year-ago net margin AND operating margin below year-ago operating
274	  margin → "Margin Compression" −3.
275	- **FR-044**: Capped or missing growth never triggers a decline penalty.
276	
277	**Total and label**
278	
279	- **FR-050**: Total = raw earned ÷ raw available × 100 over all items (penalties included in earned,
280	  adding 0 to available), rounded to the nearest integer with ties to even, then limited to 0–100.
281	  If nothing is available the total is 0.
282	- **FR-051**: The label is SUSPICIOUS when net profit margin is missing, or when Piotroski, Altman Z
283	  and Beneish M are all missing. The reason lists every condition met.
284	- **FR-052**: Otherwise: ≥70 STRONG BUY; ≥55 BUY; ≥40 HOLD; ≥25 SELL; otherwise STRONG SELL.
285	- **FR-053**: A STRONG BUY or BUY becomes INSUFFICIENT DATA when any of Forensic Quality, Growth,
286	  Revenue Quality or Competitive Moat has 0 available points.
287	- **FR-054**: Otherwise, a STRONG BUY or BUY becomes HOLD when the quality gate fails. The gate fails
288	  only on: ROE missing, ROE < 12%, or Piotroski < 4. It has no red-flag check. The reason lists every
289	  failed check.
290	- **FR-055**: The result MUST report the label before gating, the final label and the reasons, and
291	  the total MUST be the same whatever the label.
292	
293	**Valuation**
294	
295	- **FR-060**: Valuation (0–10) = P/E points + P/B points + PEG points, each 0 when missing:
296	  P/E <12 → 5, <18 → 3, <25 → 2, <50 → 1, else 0; P/B <1.5 → 3, <3.0 → 2, else 0;
297	  PEG <1 → 2, <1.5 → 1, else 0. It never affects the quality total or label.
298	
299	**Output and interface**
300	
301	- **FR-070**: The result MUST contain the total, maximum (100), raw earned and available points,
302	  each dimension with its items (name, input value, earned, available, reason), the penalties, the
303	  pre-gate and final labels with reasons, and the valuation score with its three parts.
304	- **FR-071**: The result MUST be structured data that serialises the same way every time.
305	- **FR-072**: A command-line entry point MUST score a snapshot read from a file and print the result;
306	  on invalid input it prints the error and exits with a non-zero status.
307	
308	### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
309	
310	- **Company Snapshot**: one company's metrics at one point in time. Fields (all optional):
311	  - Forensic: `piotroski` (integer 0–9), `altman_z`, `beneish_m`
312	  - 12-month totals, ₹ crore: `revenue_12m`, `revenue_prior_12m`, `ebitda_12m`, `ebitda_prior_12m`,
313	    `net_profit_12m`, `net_profit_prior_12m`
314	  - Balance sheet: `equity`, `equity_prior` (₹ crore), `debt_to_equity`, `debt_to_equity_prior`
315	    (ratios), `current_ratio` (ratio, ≥ 0)
316	  - Cash flow: `ocf_to_net_profit` (ratio)
317	  - Margins and returns, %: `net_profit_margin`, `operating_margin`, `net_profit_margin_year_ago`,
318	    `operating_margin_year_ago`, `previous_net_profit_margin`, `roe`, `roce`
319	  - Margin periods: `previous_net_profit_margin` is the net margin of the quarter immediately
320	    before the one `net_profit_margin` describes (the reference's Loss → Profit item compares the
321	    latest and previous quarterly rows, `GIS_REFERENCE.md` §3.7). `net_profit_margin_year_ago` and
322	    `operating_margin_year_ago` are the net and operating margins of the same quarter one year
323	    earlier than the one `net_profit_margin` and `operating_margin` describe (FR-043).
324	  - `recent_net_profit_margins`: list of quarterly net margins %, newest first, at most 8
325	  - Working capital, days: `ccc_days`, `ccc_days_prior`, `dso_days`, `dso_days_prior`
326	  - Valuation: `pe`, `pb`, `peg`
327	  - TTM net profit sign is taken from `net_profit_12m`.
328	  - Ranges: `piotroski` integer 0–9 (a whole-number value such as 6.0 is accepted as 6); booleans are not numeric in any field; `current_ratio` ≥ 0; `recent_net_profit_margins` at most 8
329	    numbers; every other field any finite number.
330	- **Score Item**: name, input value, points earned, points available, reason.
331	- **Dimension**: name, its items, earned and available subtotals.
332	- **Score Result**: total, raw points, dimensions, penalties, labels and reasons, valuation.
333	
334	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
335	
336	### Measurable Outcomes
337	
338	- **SC-001**: Every acceptance scenario in this spec passes as an automated test (100%).
339	- **SC-002**: Every threshold in FR-010 to FR-060 has a test on each side of its boundary; coverage of
340	  the scoring rules is 100% of lines and branches.
341	- **SC-003**: Scoring the same snapshot 1,000 times yields 1,000 identical results.
342	- **SC-004**: At least 5 worked examples, hand-computed from the reference method, produce exactly the
343	  expected total, label and valuation.
344	- **SC-005**: 10,000 snapshots are scored in under 5 seconds on a standard laptop.
345	- **SC-006**: A reviewer can trace every scoring constant in the implementation to one numbered
346	  requirement in this spec.
347	
348	## Assumptions
349	
350	- **Scope: non-financial companies only** (confirmed 2026-11-22). Banks, NBFCs and insurers (with
351	  their own KPI blocks and exemptions) are out of scope for this version.
352	- **Out of scope** (confirmed 2026-11-22): sector-percentile thresholds (scoring ladders are
353	  fixed), Capital Deployment and its re-weighting, red-flag penalties, other-income divergence,
354	  core-profit substitution, growth acceleration, the QoQ momentum items, NPM-improving-YoY, and any
355	  database or data fetching. Callers supply pre-computed metrics. Without Capital Deployment, the reference keeps its original weights,
356	  so the weights above are the reference's un-reweighted ones.
357	- **Intentional deviations from the reference**, recorded per Constitution II:
358	  - A stored 0 for ROE/ROCE/P/E/P/B/PEG is scored as 0; the reference treats it as missing (an
359	    `or` fallback). Constitution IV requires zero to be a real value.
360	  - Invalid inputs are rejected; the reference silently turns them into "missing".
361	  - When TTM profit is unknown, a non-positive cash-flow ratio scores 0; the reference then falls back
362	    to the sign of a half-year cash flow that is not an input here.
363	  - The quality gate omits two of the reference's gate conditions (`GIS_REFERENCE.md` §4, display
364	    gating): the "high-severity red flag" check, because red flags are out of scope, and the
365	    "capital-deployment redFlag" check, because red flags and Capital Deployment are both out of
366	    scope.
367	  - The SUSPICIOUS rule's "both margins missing" condition is covered by "net margin missing".
368	- Maximum available points when every input is present: 97 (Forensic 20, Growth 15, Revenue 10,
369	  Financial Health 10, Profitability 7, Moat 10, Turnaround 15, Balance Sheet 10).
370	- Units: money in ₹ crore, margins/growth/returns in percent (15 means 15%), days in days.
371	- The reference method is documented in `Assignment-1/GIS_REFERENCE.md`.

# Feature Specification: GIS Scorer (deterministic General Investor Score)

**Feature Branch**: `001-gis-scorer`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "A new, small, deterministic module that re-implements the General
Investor Score (GIS) method from myportfolio-web: given one company's pre-computed financial
metrics, return a 0–100 quality score, its per-dimension breakdown, a recommendation label and a
separate 0–10 valuation score. Scope is the subset of GIS that can be computed from explicit inputs
alone (see GIS_REFERENCE.md §7)."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-11-22

Decisions confirmed by the project owner (Balaji); non-interactive session.

- Q: Which companies and which parts of the reference GIS method are in scope? → A: Non-financial
  companies only (banks, NBFCs and insurers are out of scope). Scoring ladders are fixed, with no
  sector-percentile thresholds. Out of scope: Capital Deployment and its re-weighting, red-flag
  penalties, other-income divergence, core-profit substitution, growth acceleration, the QoQ
  momentum items, NPM-improving-YoY, and any database or data fetching.
- Q: Is an input of exactly zero a real value or missing data? → A: Zero is a real value and is
  scored as such, including ROE, ROCE, P/E, P/B and PEG; only an absent value is missing.
- Q: What happens when the input is invalid (unknown field, non-numeric, non-finite or out of
  range)? → A: Scoring is refused with an error that names the field.
- Q: What makes the quality gate fail, and does it include a red-flag check? → A: There is no
  red-flag check; the gate fails only on ROE missing, ROE < 12%, or Piotroski < 4.
- Q: How is the total rounded to a whole number? → A: To the nearest integer, ties to even.
- Q: Is an explicit null the same as an omitted field, and what do a null element or an empty list
  in `recent_net_profit_margins` mean? → A: Explicit null is the same as absent (missing). A null
  element stops the run of consecutive profitable quarters. An empty list means no quarter was
  supplied, so Profitability Sustainability is 0 of 0. (Raised by /speckit-clarify; confirmed by
  Balaji in the project thread, 2026-11-22.)
- Q: Does a whole-number float count as an integer for Piotroski, and are booleans numeric? → A:
  `6.0` is accepted as 6; `6.5` is rejected; booleans are rejected as non-numeric in every field.
  (Raised by /speckit-clarify; confirmed by Balaji in the project thread, 2026-11-22.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

The user is an analyst (or a program acting for one) who has a company's financial metrics and
wants a reproducible, explainable quality score for it.

### User Story 1 - Score a company and get its total (Priority: P1)

The analyst supplies one company's metric snapshot and receives a total score from 0 to 100, plus
a breakdown showing, for every scoring item, the points earned, the points available, and the
rule that was applied.

**Why this priority**: The total and its breakdown are the core of the method; every other story
builds on them.

**Independent Test**: Supply a complete snapshot with known values and check every item's points,
each dimension's subtotal and the normalised total against hand-computed figures.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a snapshot where every input is present and every item earns its maximum,
   **When** it is scored, **Then** the total is 100 and no penalty is listed.
2. **Given** a snapshot with Piotroski 6, Altman Z 2.5 and Beneish M −2.5, **When** it is scored,
   **Then** Forensic Quality shows 7/10, 3/5 and 5/5 (15 of 20).
3. **Given** revenue for the last 12 months of 115 against 100 for the 12 months before,
   **When** it is scored, **Then** revenue growth is 15% and earns 7 of 10.
4. **Given** a snapshot whose prior-12-month EBITDA is 0, **When** it is scored, **Then** EBITDA
   growth is reported as "capped" and earns the fixed 4 of 8, and no EBITDA decline penalty applies.
5. **Given** raw points of 45 earned out of 90 available, **When** the total is computed,
   **Then** the total is 50.

---

### User Story 2 - Missing data is excluded, never zeroed (Priority: P1)

The analyst often has incomplete data. A missing metric must not drag the score down as if it were
zero; it must drop out of both the earned and the available points, and the breakdown must say
"no data" for it.

**Why this priority**: Wrong handling of missing data silently corrupts every score, so it is as
critical as scoring itself.

**Independent Test**: Score the same snapshot with and without one input; the item disappears from
the available points and the total is re-normalised over what remains.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a snapshot with no Altman Z value, **When** it is scored, **Then** the Altman item
   shows 0 of 0 with reason "No data" and Forensic Quality is out of 15, not 20.
2. **Given** a snapshot with ROE exactly 0, **When** it is scored, **Then** ROE is scored as a real
   value (0 of 5), not treated as missing.
3. **Given** a snapshot where nothing at all can be scored, **When** it is scored, **Then** the
   total is 0 and the label is SUSPICIOUS.
4. **Given** an input that is not a number, is infinite, or is outside its allowed range (for
   example Piotroski 11), **When** it is scored, **Then** scoring is refused with an error naming
   the field, and no partial result is returned.

---

### User Story 3 - Get a recommendation label I can trust (Priority: P2)

The analyst wants a plain label (STRONG BUY … STRONG SELL) derived from the total, but a positive
label must not be shown when the data behind it is thin or the business fails basic quality checks.

**Why this priority**: The label is what most users read; it depends on the total being right first.

**Independent Test**: Feed totals on each side of each label boundary, then positive-band snapshots
that are missing a core dimension or fail the quality gate.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** totals of 70, 69, 55, 54, 40, 39, 25 and 24 with complete data that passes the quality
   gate, **When** labelled,
   **Then** the labels are STRONG BUY, BUY, BUY, HOLD, HOLD, SELL, SELL, STRONG SELL.
2. **Given** a total of 80 but no ROE and no ROCE, **When** labelled, **Then** the label is
   INSUFFICIENT DATA and the reason names the missing dimension.
3. **Given** a total of 80 with complete data and ROE 10%, **When** labelled, **Then** the label is
   HOLD and the reason says ROE is below 12%.
4. **Given** a snapshot with no net profit margin, **When** labelled, **Then** the label is
   SUSPICIOUS whatever the total.
5. **Given** a total of 30, missing ROE and ROCE, **When** labelled, **Then** the label stays SELL
   (gates only ever downgrade positive labels).

---

### User Story 4 - Penalties for a deteriorating business (Priority: P2)

The analyst wants declining revenue, earnings or EBITDA, and shrinking margins, to cost points,
and wants to see each penalty listed.

**Why this priority**: Penalties change the total materially and are a frequent source of disputes.

**Independent Test**: Score a snapshot with declining figures and check each penalty line and the
effect on the total.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** revenue growth of −2%, **When** scored, **Then** a "Revenue Declining" penalty of −5
   is listed and revenue growth itself earns 0 of 10.
2. **Given** net margin 8% vs 9% a year earlier and operating margin 12% vs 13% a year earlier,
   **When** scored, **Then** a "Margin Compression" penalty of −3 is listed.
3. **Given** only one of the two margins below its year-ago value, **When** scored, **Then** no
   Margin Compression penalty is listed.
4. **Given** penalties that push raw points below zero, **When** the total is computed, **Then** the
   total is 0, never negative.

---

### User Story 5 - Separate valuation score (Priority: P3)

The analyst wants a 0–10 valuation score from P/E, P/B and PEG, reported separately so price never
changes the quality score.

**Why this priority**: Useful context, but independent of the quality score.

**Independent Test**: Score P/E, P/B and PEG values on each side of each band and check the sum.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** P/E 11, P/B 1.4 and PEG 0.9, **When** valued, **Then** the valuation score is 10.
2. **Given** P/E 60, P/B 4 and PEG 2, **When** valued, **Then** the valuation score is 0.
3. **Given** no P/E, P/B or PEG, **When** valued, **Then** the valuation score is 0 and the quality
   total is unchanged.

---

### User Story 6 - Run it from the command line (Priority: P3)

The analyst wants to score a snapshot stored in a file without writing code, and get the result
as structured output.

**Why this priority**: Convenience for the harness and demos; the library is the product.

**Independent Test**: Run the command on a sample snapshot file and compare its output with the
library's result for the same input.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a valid snapshot file, **When** the command is run on it, **Then** it prints the result
   as structured data and exits successfully.
2. **Given** an invalid snapshot file, **When** the command is run on it, **Then** it prints the
   validation error and exits with a failure status.

---

### Edge Cases

- A growth base (prior 12 months) of zero or negative → the item is "capped" (fixed mid points),
  never a division by zero, and no decline penalty applies to it.
- Current value more than 4× its base → "capped" (a recovery or base effect, not real growth).
- Exactly 4× the base → not capped (the cap test is strictly greater than 4×); values are rounded to
  6 decimal places before this test so tiny floating-point noise cannot flip it.
- Negative current value against a positive base → normal growth (negative %), scored and penalised.
- Total exactly on a half point (e.g. 72.5) → rounded half to even (72), matching the reference.
- Operating cash flow ÷ net profit below 0 while TTM profit is positive → −3 (worse than 0).
  The same ratio when TTM profit is a loss or unknown, or a ratio of exactly 0 → 0.
- A negative P/E (loss-making company) is scored as given, so it falls in the cheapest band; callers
  should pass P/E as missing for a loss-maker, as the reference's data does.
- D/E below 0.5 in both years → Debt Reduction is not applicable (0 of 0), not 0 of 3.
- Working capital with only CCC or only DSO available → the missing change counts as 0 and the
  item is still scored; with neither → 0 of 0.
- Profitability Sustainability with fewer than 2 quarters supplied → 0 of 2 (scored, not missing)
  unless no quarter is supplied at all.
- Piotroski must be an integer 0–9; anything else is an input error.
- An unknown field name, a non-numeric value, a non-finite value (NaN, ±infinity) or an
  out-of-range value → scoring is refused with an error naming the field; nothing is scored.
- ROE or ROCE of exactly 0 → scored as 0 of 5 (not missing). P/E, P/B or PEG of exactly 0 → scored
  in its lowest band (P/E 5, P/B 3, PEG 2), not treated as missing.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

**Inputs and validation**

- **FR-001**: The system MUST accept one company snapshot made of the named metrics in the Key
  Entities section. Every metric is optional; only an absent value (or an explicit null, which is the same) means "missing". Zero is a real
  value and is scored as such for every metric, including ROE, ROCE, P/E, P/B and PEG.
- **FR-002**: The system MUST reject a snapshot containing an unknown field, a non-numeric value, a
  non-finite value, or a value outside its stated range, with an error that names the field.
- **FR-003**: The system MUST produce identical output for identical input, with no dependence on
  time, environment, files, network or randomness.

**Item scoring**: each item yields points earned, points available and a reason. A missing input
gives 0 of 0 with reason "No data". All boundaries below are exact.

- **FR-010 Piotroski F-score** (available 10): ≥8 → 10; ≥6 → 7; ≥4 → 4; ≥2 → 2; otherwise 0.
- **FR-011 Altman Z** (5): >2.99 → 5; ≥1.81 → 3; otherwise 0.
- **FR-012 Beneish M** (5): <−2.22 → 5; ≤−1.78 → 2; otherwise 0.
- **FR-013 Growth calculation**: For revenue, EBITDA and net profit, growth % =
  (current 12M − prior 12M) ÷ |prior 12M| × 100, both values first rounded to 6 decimals. If the
  prior 12M is ≤ 0, or the current 12M is > 0 and greater than 4 × prior 12M, the growth is
  "capped" and no percentage is reported. If either value is missing, growth is missing.
- **FR-014 EBITDA growth** (8): ≥20% → 8; ≥15 → 6; ≥10 → 4; ≥5 → 2; otherwise 0. Capped → 4 of 8.
- **FR-015 Earnings (net profit) growth** (7): ≥20% → 7; ≥10 → 5; ≥5 → 3; ≥0 → 2; otherwise 0.
  Capped → 3 of 7.
- **FR-016 Revenue growth** (10): ≥25% → 10; ≥15 → 7; ≥10 → 5; ≥0 → 3; otherwise 0.
  Capped → 5 of 10.
- **FR-017 Equity growth** (5), from current and prior equity, growth = (current − prior) ÷ |prior|
  × 100, missing if prior is 0: >15% → 5; ≥10 → 3; ≥5 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-018 Cash-flow quality** (5), operating cash flow ÷ net profit: ≥1.5 → 5; ≥1.0 → 4; ≥0.8 → 3;
  ≥0.5 → 2; >0 → 1; <0 with TTM net profit (`net_profit_12m`) > 0 → −3; otherwise 0.
- **FR-019 Net profit margin** (3): >15% → 3; >10 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-020 Operating margin** (4): >20% → 4; >15 → 3; >10 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-021 ROE and ROCE** (5 each): ≥15% → 5; ≥12 → 3; ≥8 → 2; >0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-022 Loss → Profit transition** (5): available when current and previous net margin are both
  present; 5 when current > 0 and previous ≤ 0, otherwise 0.
- **FR-023 Profitability sustainability** (2): count the consecutive quarters, newest first, with net
  margin > 0 (stopping at the first that is not, or is missing); ≥4 → 2; ≥2 → 1; otherwise 0.
  Missing only when no quarterly margin is supplied (field absent, null, or an empty list).
- **FR-024 Working-capital efficiency** (5): ΔCCC = current − prior CCC days; ΔDSO = current − prior
  DSO days; a change that cannot be computed counts as 0, and the item is missing when neither can.
  ΔCCC ≤ −300 or ΔDSO ≤ −40 → 5; ΔCCC ≤ −150 or ΔDSO ≤ −25 → 4; ΔCCC ≤ −75 or ΔDSO ≤ −12 → 3;
  ΔCCC ≤ −30 or ΔDSO ≤ −5 → 2; ΔCCC < 0 or ΔDSO < 0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-025 Debt reduction** (3): needs current and prior D/E. If both are < 0.5 → 0 of 0 ("not
  applicable"). Otherwise ΔD/E = current − prior: ≤ −0.5 → 3; ≤ −0.2 → 2; < 0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-026 Current ratio** (5): >2.0 → 5; ≥1.5 → 3; ≥1.0 → 1; otherwise 0.
- **FR-027 Debt-to-equity level** (5): <0.5 → 5; ≤1.0 → 3; ≤2.0 → 1; otherwise 0.

**Dimensions**

- **FR-030**: Items MUST be grouped and reported in this order:
  Forensic Quality (FR-010–012), Growth (FR-014–015), Revenue Quality (FR-016),
  Financial Health (FR-017–018), Profitability (FR-019–020), Competitive Moat (FR-021),
  Turnaround (FR-022–025), Balance Sheet (FR-026–027), Penalties (FR-040–043).
  Each dimension reports the sum of its items' earned and available points.

**Penalties**: points < 0 with 0 available.

- **FR-040**: Revenue growth < 0 → "Revenue Declining" −5.
- **FR-041**: Earnings growth < 0 → "Earnings Declining" −5.
- **FR-042**: EBITDA growth < 0 → "EBITDA Declining" −5.
- **FR-043**: Net margin below year-ago net margin AND operating margin below year-ago operating
  margin → "Margin Compression" −3.
- **FR-044**: Capped or missing growth never triggers a decline penalty.

**Total and label**

- **FR-050**: Total = raw earned ÷ raw available × 100 over all items (penalties included in earned,
  adding 0 to available), rounded to the nearest integer with ties to even, then limited to 0–100.
  If nothing is available the total is 0.
- **FR-051**: The label is SUSPICIOUS when net profit margin is missing, or when Piotroski, Altman Z
  and Beneish M are all missing. The reason lists every condition met.
- **FR-052**: Otherwise: ≥70 STRONG BUY; ≥55 BUY; ≥40 HOLD; ≥25 SELL; otherwise STRONG SELL.
- **FR-053**: A STRONG BUY or BUY becomes INSUFFICIENT DATA when any of Forensic Quality, Growth,
  Revenue Quality or Competitive Moat has 0 available points.
- **FR-054**: Otherwise, a STRONG BUY or BUY becomes HOLD when the quality gate fails. The gate fails
  only on: ROE missing, ROE < 12%, or Piotroski < 4. It has no red-flag check. The reason lists every
  failed check.
- **FR-055**: The result MUST report the label before gating, the final label and the reasons, and
  the total MUST be the same whatever the label.

**Valuation**

- **FR-060**: Valuation (0–10) = P/E points + P/B points + PEG points, each 0 when missing:
  P/E <12 → 5, <18 → 3, <25 → 2, <50 → 1, else 0; P/B <1.5 → 3, <3.0 → 2, else 0;
  PEG <1 → 2, <1.5 → 1, else 0. It never affects the quality total or label.

**Output and interface**

- **FR-070**: The result MUST contain the total, maximum (100), raw earned and available points,
  each dimension with its items (name, input value, earned, available, reason), the penalties, the
  pre-gate and final labels with reasons, and the valuation score with its three parts.
- **FR-071**: The result MUST be structured data that serialises the same way every time.
- **FR-072**: A command-line entry point MUST score a snapshot read from a file and print the result;
  on invalid input it prints the error and exits with a non-zero status.

### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*

- **Company Snapshot**: one company's metrics at one point in time. Fields (all optional):
  - Forensic: `piotroski` (integer 0–9), `altman_z`, `beneish_m`
  - 12-month totals, ₹ crore: `revenue_12m`, `revenue_prior_12m`, `ebitda_12m`, `ebitda_prior_12m`,
    `net_profit_12m`, `net_profit_prior_12m`
  - Balance sheet: `equity`, `equity_prior` (₹ crore), `debt_to_equity`, `debt_to_equity_prior`
    (ratios), `current_ratio` (ratio, ≥ 0)
  - Cash flow: `ocf_to_net_profit` (ratio)
  - Margins and returns, %: `net_profit_margin`, `operating_margin`, `net_profit_margin_year_ago`,
    `operating_margin_year_ago`, `previous_net_profit_margin`, `roe`, `roce`
  - Margin periods: `previous_net_profit_margin` is the net margin of the quarter immediately
    before the one `net_profit_margin` describes (the reference's Loss → Profit item compares the
    latest and previous quarterly rows, `GIS_REFERENCE.md` §3.7). `net_profit_margin_year_ago` and
    `operating_margin_year_ago` are the net and operating margins of the same quarter one year
    earlier than the one `net_profit_margin` and `operating_margin` describe (FR-043).
  - `recent_net_profit_margins`: list of quarterly net margins %, newest first, at most 8
  - Working capital, days: `ccc_days`, `ccc_days_prior`, `dso_days`, `dso_days_prior`
  - Valuation: `pe`, `pb`, `peg`
  - TTM net profit sign is taken from `net_profit_12m`.
  - Ranges: `piotroski` integer 0–9 (a whole-number value such as 6.0 is accepted as 6); booleans are not numeric in any field; `current_ratio` ≥ 0; `recent_net_profit_margins` at most 8
    numbers; every other field any finite number.
- **Score Item**: name, input value, points earned, points available, reason.
- **Dimension**: name, its items, earned and available subtotals.
- **Score Result**: total, raw points, dimensions, penalties, labels and reasons, valuation.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Every acceptance scenario in this spec passes as an automated test (100%).
- **SC-002**: Every threshold in FR-010 to FR-060 has a test on each side of its boundary; coverage of
  the scoring rules is 100% of lines and branches.
- **SC-003**: Scoring the same snapshot 1,000 times yields 1,000 identical results.
- **SC-004**: At least 5 worked examples, hand-computed from the reference method, produce exactly the
  expected total, label and valuation.
- **SC-005**: 10,000 snapshots are scored in under 5 seconds on a standard laptop.
- **SC-006**: A reviewer can trace every scoring constant in the implementation to one numbered
  requirement in this spec.

## Assumptions

- **Scope: non-financial companies only** (confirmed 2026-11-22). Banks, NBFCs and insurers (with
  their own KPI blocks and exemptions) are out of scope for this version.
- **Out of scope** (confirmed 2026-11-22): sector-percentile thresholds (scoring ladders are
  fixed), Capital Deployment and its re-weighting, red-flag penalties, other-income divergence,
  core-profit substitution, growth acceleration, the QoQ momentum items, NPM-improving-YoY, and any
  database or data fetching. Callers supply pre-computed metrics. Without Capital Deployment, the reference keeps its original weights,
  so the weights above are the reference's un-reweighted ones.
- **Intentional deviations from the reference**, recorded per Constitution II:
  - A stored 0 for ROE/ROCE/P/E/P/B/PEG is scored as 0; the reference treats it as missing (an
    `or` fallback). Constitution IV requires zero to be a real value.
  - Invalid inputs are rejected; the reference silently turns them into "missing".
  - When TTM profit is unknown, a non-positive cash-flow ratio scores 0; the reference then falls back
    to the sign of a half-year cash flow that is not an input here.
  - The quality gate omits two of the reference's gate conditions (`GIS_REFERENCE.md` §4, display
    gating): the "high-severity red flag" check, because red flags are out of scope, and the
    "capital-deployment redFlag" check, because red flags and Capital Deployment are both out of
    scope.
  - The SUSPICIOUS rule's "both margins missing" condition is covered by "net margin missing".
- Maximum available points when every input is present: 97 (Forensic 20, Growth 15, Revenue 10,
  Financial Health 10, Profitability 7, Moat 10, Turnaround 15, Balance Sheet 10).
- Units: money in ₹ crore, margins/growth/returns in percent (15 means 15%), days in days.
- The reference method is documented in `Assignment-1/GIS_REFERENCE.md`.
